points.point: Conway-Bogue (1957): brokers may fill in standard forms only in transactions they broker, with no fee beyond the commission
C.R.S. 12-10-403(4): a Commission-approved form must be used whenever one exists and fits the transaction
Brokers may not prepare documents for deals they aren't brokering, charge a document fee, or draft legal language
The eight kinds of standard forms and their limits (e.g. a letter of intent must say it is nonbinding)
Builder/bank/principal-supplied contracts: insert transaction facts only and advise the client in writing to see an attorney
A broker who is a party must disclose licensed status in writing
Printed text is deleted only by negotiation or instruction, struck through so it stays legible
Other form changes: inapplicable sections keep their caption marked N/A; inserted text stands out; every change explained
Additional Provisions record agreed facts only; legal drafting goes to an attorney
Attorney-drafted clauses are kept, with the attorney's name, 4 years from last use
A broker who isn't a party may not add an exculpatory clause protecting the broker
Match the contract to the property's use (Residential, Income-Residential, Commercial, Land, CBSF1, MHC1)
There are no Commission-approved leases or property management agreements
Forms are revised with mandatory-use dates; using an outdated version is a violation
The property is identified by legal description; a street address alone isn't enough
Attached items are included unless excluded; list an exclusion to keep a fixture
Leased items and encumbered inclusions need the buyer's election to assume and lessor/lienholder approval
Water rights have their own subsection and Water Rights Examination Deadline
A seller concession is a credit to the buyer at closing for lender-allowed costs
Earnest money is delivered with the contract (unless an Alternative Earnest Money Deadline) and held in trust by the Earnest Money Holder
The party who isn't entitled must sign the Earnest Money Release within 3 days or be in default
Counting days: exclude the first day, include the last
A day ends 11:59 p.m. MT; weekend/holiday deadlines don't move unless 'Will' is checked
The Time of Day Deadline applies to objection, resolution, examination and termination deadlines
A blank, N/A or Deleted deadline means the deadline and its provision don't apply
Time is of the essence: late notices are ineffective and the right is waived
Acceptance requires both signatures and the offering party's receipt of notice by the Acceptance Deadline
New Loan Terms Deadline: buyer may terminate over unsatisfactory loan terms
New Loan Availability Deadline: underwriting problems only; no timely notice makes earnest money nonrefundable
Seller or private financing: either party may terminate by the Seller or Private Financing Deadline
Low or late appraisal: buyer may terminate or object by the Appraisal Objection Deadline
An unresolved appraisal objection terminates the contract at the Appraisal Resolution Deadline unless withdrawn
FHA and VA loans have their own appraisal language; the contract's appraisal deadlines don't apply
No box checked: seller selects the title company and pays for the owner's policy
Owner's Extended Coverage removes standard exceptions for unrecorded matters
Record title: a buyer who doesn't object by the deadline accepts title as shown
Off-record title covers unrecorded easements, boundary disputes and parties in possession
An unresolved title objection terminates the contract at the Title Resolution Deadline unless withdrawn
New ILC or survey: buyer may terminate or object by the New ILC or New Survey Objection Deadline
Association documents at seller's expense; late delivery gives the buyer 10 days after receipt
Seller requests the status letter (14+ days before closing) and pays its fee
The Seller's Property Disclosure is completed by the seller from current actual knowledge; not a warranty
Continuing duty to disclose new adverse facts; buyer may terminate by earlier of closing or 5 days
Lead-based paint disclosure for dwellings built or permitted before 1978
Methamphetamine disclosure unless remediated to state standards
Radon advisory recommends testing; seller provides known test results
Buyer acknowledges source-of-water and well permit information
Carbon monoxide alarms within 15 feet of each bedroom entrance
Inspection Termination Deadline: buyer may simply terminate if no objection was delivered
Inspection objection unresolved by the Inspection Resolution Deadline terminates the contract unless withdrawn
Buyer pays for inspections, repairs inspection damage and indemnifies the seller; this survives termination
Conditional sale and due diligence documents: buyer must act by the deadline or lose the right
Default deed is a special warranty deed
Seller holding over after possession faces eviction, per-day amount and damages; stays use a Post-Closing Occupancy Agreement
Casualty damage over 10% of price (or unrepaired) lets the buyer terminate
Taxes are paid in arrears: seller credits the buyer for the seller's share at closing
Prorations are to the Closing Date and are final unless Additional Provisions say otherwise
Buyer default with specific performance box unchecked: earnest money as liquidated damages is the seller's only remedy
Seller default: buyer may cancel and recover earnest money and damages, or sue for specific performance
Mediation is required first; duty ends 30 days after the written request
Earnest money dispute: holder may hold, interplead, or return to buyer absent a case number within 120 days
Termination is effective on receipt; earnest money returns to the buyer unless the buyer is in default
The Counterproposal lists only changes; blank or 'No Change' keeps a term, 'Deleted' removes it
A new Counterproposal supersedes and replaces any earlier one
Acceptance requires the offering party to receive notice by the deadline
A counteroffer rejects the original offer, which can't be accepted later
Changes after signing use the Agreement to Amend/Extend, signed by both parties
A terminated contract can't be amended; use the Agreement to Revive Contract
Extension or Termination of Contract: if Part I isn't accepted in time, Part II is the requester's notice to terminate
Notice forms (objection notices, Inspection Resolution, Notice to Terminate, Earnest Money Release); give the lender a copy of an Inspection Resolution
Notices are written, effective on receipt, and delivery to the party's broker counts (except after closing)
Electronic notice and delivery are allowed; timing turns on receipt and any Time of Day Deadline
A seller's agent presents all offers timely, even when the property is under contract
Limits on which offers are presented must follow an explanation and be written into the listing
If the listing broker won't respond, go to the employing broker before the seller
No box checked = no consent to disclose that other offers exist; terms always need written consent
Without informed consent, the seller's agent may not disclose that the seller would take less
A second accepted offer should be a backup contingent on the first contract terminating
Countering several buyers at once risks more than one binding contract
Exclusive Right-to-Sell: no relationship box checked means transaction-brokerage
Compensation is earned if the property sells during the listing by anyone, including the seller
Third-party compensation requires the seller's written consent
Holdover covers Submitted Prospects named to the seller in writing during the listing
Holdover double-commission box: if unchecked, the seller doesn't owe the first firm when a new firm earns a fee
Exclusive Right-to-Buy: compensation negotiable; buyer owes unpaid balance only if disclosed in writing before the purchase contract
Exclusive Right-to-Buy Megan's Law paragraph: buyer gets offender information from local law enforcement
The Seller's Property Disclosure is completed by the seller, not the broker
The broker separately discloses adverse material facts the broker actually knows
Square Footage Disclosure is completed by the listing licensee and is for marketing only
Source of Water Addendum: well permit number, provider contact, or other source
Lead-based paint: pre-1978, EPA pamphlet, 10-day risk-assessment opportunity
Short Sale Addendum: contract terminates without lienholder acceptance by the Short Sale Acceptance Deadline
Short sale seller may still owe the deficiency unless released in writing; forgiven debt can be taxable
CBSF1 is required when an owner-occupant in foreclosure sells to a non-occupant equity purchaser
CBSF1 can't be used with an assumption, leaseback or repurchase option; an attorney prepares that contract
Foreclosure Protection Act cancellation: earlier of midnight of the 3rd business day or noon the day before the sale
Closing Instructions are signed by buyer, seller and closing company
Closing company prepares standard statutory deeds; personal representative's, trustee's and nonstandard deeds come from attorneys
Brokers may fill in Commission note and deed of trust forms in their own transactions, with no extra fee
Deed of trust versions: Strict, Creditworthy, Assumable; the county Public Trustee is the trustee
Brokers don't advise on or draft financing terms; consumer credit deals go to an attorney or licensed MLO
Income-Residential (CBS2) for rental and investment residential property
Commercial (CBS3) for office, retail, industrial and mixed use, with environmental and ADA due diligence
Land (CBS4) for vacant/agricultural land; no farm and ranch contract; Residential Addendum when dwellings are present
CBSF1 applies to owner-occupied homes in foreclosure sold to non-occupant buyers
CBSF1 deal must be clean: no assumption, leaseback or buy-back, nothing of value before cancellation expires
Manufactured home on a rented park space uses the Lot Lease Only contract
Under MHC1, title passes by certificate of title and the buyer applies to the Department of Revenue
MHC1 depends on the park owner's written approval and lease assignment or new lease
Manufactured home sold with land uses the Land or Commercial contract plus the Manufactured Home Addendum
No Commission lease: the firm's own attorney drafts it or the owner supplies it
Exclusive Right-to-Lease Listing Contract is the landlord-side leasing listing
Property management: attorney-drafted agreement plus the Brokerage Duties Addendum
Assignment of Lease moves the landlord's lease rights and deposits to the buyer at closing
Licensee Buy-Out Addendum is used when a licensee buys the client's property
Buy-out seller may terminate anytime and reimburses out-of-pocket expenses up to a cap
Guaranteed buy-out property keeps being marketed as active
Post-Closing Occupancy Agreement is limited to 60 days
PCOA terms: rent in advance, buyer holds deposit (max two months' rent) and returns it within 30 days
Pre-closing occupancy has no Commission form; use an attorney
Source of Water Addendum records well, provider or other source
Short Sale Addenda (listing and purchase): terminate without lender acceptance by the deadline
Exchange Addendum: cooperation at no cost or liability; exchange isn't a condition of the contract
Non-Commission forms only when none fits; a broker-party's attorney form must say it is not Commission-approved
Forms are revised often; confirm the current version and mandatory-use date
A common interest community obligates owners to pay for common property or other units' expenses
CCIOA applies to communities created on or after July 1, 1992, with limited sections reaching older ones
CCIOA protections can't be waived and limit what HOAs can prohibit
The recorded declaration creates the community and is the top governing document
No fines without a written fine policy giving notice and a hearing
Regular vs. special assessments
The HOA lien is perfected by recording the declaration and lapses without enforcement within 6 years
Statement of unpaid assessments due within 14 calendar days; binding; failure bars the lien as of the request date
Super-lien: up to six months of regular assessments beat a first deed of trust; taxes still come first
Foreclosure needs a balance of at least six months' assessments and a recorded board vote; fines alone can't support it
An unregistered association can't enforce its lien until it re-registers
Seller must give the CIC disclosure; failure exposes the seller to actual damages and costs
Association documents: seller provides; buyer may terminate by deadline or 10 days after late delivery
Seller requests and pays for the status letter
Special assessments: checkbox for those levied before closing; seller pays for improvements installed as of buyer's signing
No state license for HOA managers since 2019; the HOA Center is not a regulator
Brokers flag issues and calendar deadlines but don't interpret HOA documents
Conway-Bogue limits on brokers completing forms
Unauthorized practice of law: refer legal questions to an attorney
Additional Provisions: facts only, no legal drafting
Broker as principal: written license disclosure; Commission forms when selling through the firm
Choosing the right Commission contract by property use
Inclusions and fixtures stay unless excluded
Deadline mechanics: 11:59 p.m. MT and weekend default
Offers, counteroffers and acceptance
Loan termination rights (terms vs. availability)
Appraisal objection resolved by Amend/Extend before the deadline
Title insurance default and extended coverage
Unresolved title objection terminates; revive with Agreement to Revive
Seller's Property Disclosure: completed by seller; continuing duty
Inspection objection and resolution
Default deed is special warranty
Prorations and deposits at closing
Buyer and seller default remedies
Earnest money disputes
Amending a signed contract
Notice delivery and timing
Multiple offers: presenting and disclosing offers
Listing contract relationship default
Holdover protects only prospects named in writing
Lead-based paint record keeping
Short sales
Foreclosure Protection Act cancellation right
Closing Instructions signers
Seller financing forms and the Public Trustee
Manufactured home on a leased lot
Leasing forms: no Commission lease
Licensee Buy-Out Addendum
Seller rent-back vs. buyer early occupancy
Exchange Addendum
CCIOA scope
HOA super-lien and foreclosure limits
Association documents timing
CIC disclosure duty
HOA managers and the HOA Center
